definitions.explanation: Medicine prepared as a fine powder rather than as tablets or liquid. Typically dispensed in small paper packets and taken with water. Common in Japan for both prescription and over-the-counter remedies, especially cold medicines and stomach treatments.

examples.japanese: {粉薬|こなぐすり}は{苦|にが}い。
{粉薬|こなぐすり}を{水|みず}と{一緒|いっしょ}に{飲|の}んだ。
examples.english: I took the powdered medicine with water.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{粉薬|こなぐすり}を{嫌|いや}がるので、ゼリーに{混|ま}ぜて{飲|の}ませている。
examples.english: Our child hates powdered medicine, so we mix it into jelly to get him to take it.

notes:
Compound of {粉|こな} (powder) + {薬|くすり} (medicine). The {薬|くすり} voices to ぐすり through {連濁|れんだく}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {粉薬|こなぐすり}を{飲|の}む: to take powdered medicine
- {粉薬|こなぐすり}を{処方|しょほう}する: to prescribe a powder medication
- {粉薬|こなぐすり}が{苦手|にがて}: bad at taking powdered medicine

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {錠剤|じょうざい}: tablet; pill — solid medicine in a pressed form
- カプセル: capsule — powder or liquid medicine inside a soluble shell
- {水薬|すいやく}/{液剤|えきざい}: liquid medicine
